name: pinneapple_veriphysics

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.applicability
children.doc:
Applicability map: a structured evidence chain for one Veriphysics run.

Turns validation from pass/fail into an *engineering applicability map*:

* **what physics was directly verified** (tier ``VERIFIED`` -- a check
  actually executed in this run and produced a number),
* **what is only inferred from the model/design** (tier ``INFERRED`` --
  plausible given what ran, but no check measured it directly),
* **where the evidence is too sparse to support extrapolation** (tier
  ``UNSUPPORTED`` -- nothing was checked there; do not use the surrogate
  there without new evidence).

It also answers a fixed eight-item review checklist (surrogate, error,
convergence, generalization, variables, weights, uncertainty
quantification, conservation/standard physics).

Like ``decision.py`` and ``evidence_report.py`` this module never runs a
check and never invents a number: it only *classifies and renders* facts
the pipeline already produced. A check that did not run is ``NOT_RUN``,
never a neutral pass. It deliberately imports nothing from
``pinneapple_*`` so it is cheap to test and reproducible from a saved
``decision_record.json``.

(Extracted from Veriphysics' orchestrator; Apache-2.0 like the rest of PINNeAPPle. Execution queue, API and billing stay in Veriphysics.)

classes.name: Tolerances
classes.doc:
Acceptance tolerances of the applicability map (#6). The defaults are the heuristics above; a request can
replace any of them with criteria agreed for the target application. The map records which were used and
whether they came from the request.

methods.doc: The tolerances that differ from the defaults.

functions.name: build_applicability_map
functions.sig: (*, architecture: str, coords: Sequence[str], fields: Sequence[str], domain_bounds: dict[str, tuple[float, float]], physical_parameters: dict[str, float] | None, guardrail_checks: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], confidence_components: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], parameter_ranges: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None, final_loss: float | None = None, loss_history: Sequence[float] | None = None, ...
functions.doc:
Classify the facts of one run. ``heldout_error`` (optional) is
``{"metric": str, "value": float, "threshold": float, "description": str}``
from an out-of-sample test the caller ran. ``extrapolation``,
``ensemble`` and ``weight_sensitivity`` are the dicts returned by
``robustness.extrapolation_study`` / ``ensemble_study`` (minus the
``members`` models) / ``weight_sensitivity_study``. Without any of
them the corresponding item is ``NOT_RUN`` -- the guardrail residual
is evaluated on fresh points but *inside the training domain*, which
is not generalization.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.dossier
children.doc:
Validation dossier: the case, its evidence, its maturity and its decision, as one document an engineer can file.

The dossier is the artefact the loop produces -- the thing a reviewer signs, a colleague reads, or a customer's quality
process accepts as *supporting evidence*. It is deliberately plain and complete rather than persuasive: declared use,
the criteria that were set, the checks that ran (and those that did not), the reference comparisons with their
measured error against the tolerance, the domain of applicability, the uncertainty and its limitations, the expert
decisions with their scope, the maturity on both axes with what is missing, and the provenance needed to reproduce it.

It is **not** a certification: :data:`DISCLAIMER` says so on the document itself. What it establishes is narrower and
more useful -- what was verified, what was validated, for which scope, by whom, with which evidence.

::

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.dossier import ValidationDossier

    d = ValidationDossier.from_case(case)
    d.write("case.html")                      # self-contained HTML
    print(d.render_text())                    # the same content as text

classes.name: ValidationDossier
classes.doc: The document of one case at its latest revision.

methods.sig: (case: ValidationCase, assessment: CaseAssessment | None = None) -> ValidationDossier

methods.name: improvement_tasks
methods.doc: What to do next: the open requirements of both axes, lowest level first.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: Write the dossier (``html``, ``md`` or ``txt``) and return the path.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.evidence_package
children.doc:
Engineering evidence: turn experiments and simulations into a reproducible report and a zip package.

Sources are the files other tools wrote, read as they are and hashed:

=======================  ===================================================================================
``validation-lab``       a Validation Lab report (``pinneapple-validation-lab/v1``): checks and their ledger
``ledger``               an evidence ledger (``pinneapple-evidence-ledger/v1``)
``pinneapple-check``     a ``pinneapple check --json`` report (no ledger: its checks read "not run" here)
``comparator``           a Simulation Comparator result (global and per-field errors)
``contract``             a StudyResult, ModelRef or DatasetSpec (JSON with ``"type"`` or ``"contract"``)
``metrics``              a table (CSV, Parquet, JSON list of rows): one row per run/method, numeric columns
``metadata``             any other JSON object (simulation metadata, configuration)
``file``                 anything else: referenced by name, size and SHA-256
=======================  ===================================================================================

The central rule, enforced by :func:`build_report` and tested: a test is reported as passed or failed only when
an intact :class:`~pinneapple_veriphysics.ledger.EvidenceEntry` records that it ran (inputs hash, outputs, time).
A source that only says "passed" gives "not run", with the claim shown next to it.

::

    srcs = [load_source(name, data) for name, data in files]
    report = build_report({"title": "Heat sink v2", "baseline": "FEM", "candidate": "PINN"}, srcs)
    html = render_html(report, figures=make_figures(report, "out"))
    pdf = render_pdf(report, figures=make_figures(report, "out"))      # needs reportlab
    zip_bytes = build_package(report, srcs, html=html, pdf=pdf, figures=...)
    assert verify_package(zip_bytes) == []

functions.sig: (name: str, data: bytes, url: str = '') -> Source
functions.doc: Read one file and decide what it is (never fails: unknown content is kept as a referenced file).

functions.doc:
The report as data. ``meta``: title, project, author, purpose, methodology, conditions (dict),
limitations (list), baseline and candidate (labels matched against run names), references (list).

functions.sig: (report: dict[str, Any], outdir: str | Path) -> dict[str, str]
functions.doc: PNG figures from the report's own numbers: baseline vs candidate metrics, test status per group.

functions.name: render_html
functions.sig: (report: dict[str, Any], figures: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str
functions.doc: Self-contained HTML (figures inlined as PNG data URIs).

functions.name: render_pdf
functions.sig: (report: dict[str, Any], figures: dict[str, str] | None = None, path: str | Path | None = None) -> bytes
functions.doc: PDF through :class:`pinneapple_tools.reporting.paperkit.Paper` (needs reportlab).

functions.doc:
The report as a ``StudyResult`` (``pinneapple_data.contracts``, study type ``evidence``) for the next app:
one check per test (PASS / FAIL with its record as evidence, NOT_RUN otherwise), the test counts as metrics, the
artifacts by SHA-256 and the limitations as limits.

functions.sig: (report: dict[str, Any], sources: Sequence[Source], *, html: str | None = None, pdf: bytes | None = None, figures: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> bytes
functions.doc:
Zip: report.json/html/pdf, evidence-ledger.json, figures/, sources/ (the original bytes) and
MANIFEST.json with the SHA-256 of every other file.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.evidence_report
children.doc:
Evidence Report PDF generator.

This is the sprint's "Evidence Report in PDF" deliverable -- see
``helm/docs/PINNeAPPle90/sprint1/04-escopo-minimo-mvps.md``, MVP 1's
minimal flow: Formulario -> Executar -> Capturar -> Validar -> Pontuar ->
**Evidence Report em PDF**.

This module renders EXACTLY the data a (see :class:`~pinneapple_veriphysics
.decision.DecisionRecord` already carries -- the same content
``DecisionRecord.render()`` produces as plain text, plus the per-check
confidence breakdown (``DecisionRecord.confidence_components``) -- into a
PDF. It computes nothing new and imports no verification/scoring code;
every number here was already produced by
the Veriphysics orchestrator's ``analyze()``. This matches the rest of
this repo's "thin layer over already-computed data" pattern, and its
anti-fabrication discipline: a check absent from ``confidence_components``
is rendered as "not run", never a fabricated score (see
``decision.ALL_CONFIDENCE_COMPONENT_NAMES`` and README.md's
"Anti-fabrication design").

Deliberately plain: a single-column, black-on-white document with no
charts, logos, or color -- an evidence document a reviewing engineer can
scan quickly, not a marketing artifact. This matches the sprint's own
scope note ("no polish beyond what credibility requires").

(Extracted from Veriphysics' orchestrator; Apache-2.0 like the rest of PINNeAPPle. Execution queue, API and billing stay in Veriphysics.)

functions.name: render_evidence_report_pdf
functions.sig: (decision: DecisionRecord) -> bytes
functions.doc:
Render *decision* (a real, already-computed ``DecisionRecord``) as
an Evidence Report PDF and return the raw PDF bytes.

Sections, in order: problem, recommended strategy + reasoning, trust
score + coverage, guardrail verdict, the scope of use (when the record
has one: which uses the result serves and why, with its figure), the per-check confidence
breakdown (one line per check, or "not run"), alternatives considered,
external tools recommended, and the next best action -- the same
content ``DecisionRecord.render()``'s plain-text report carries, laid
out as a PDF instead of a terminal-friendly string.

children.summary: Evidence Report PDF generator.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.example_cases
children.doc:
Fixed catalog of pre-defined "example case" problems -- the "small,
fixed set of 2-3 example problem classes" the MVP 1 scope freeze requires
(``helm/docs/PINNeAPPle90/sprint1/04-escopo-minimo-mvps.md``): Burgers 1D
(already existed) plus two turbomachinery cases (added here) that run for
real through the orchestrated pipeline today, with no change to the
shared PINNeAPPle library -- see ``axial_compressor_meanline`` and
``axial_compressor_stage_3d`` in
``pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.turbomachinery``, both
100%-``callable``-selector boundary conditions (the same mechanism that
already makes ``burgers_1d`` work), unlike ``industrial_furnace_thermal``/
``pipe_flow_3d`` (``selector_type="tag"``, NOT auto-sampled by
``pinneapple_physics.solve_pde`` -- deliberately out of scope here, see
ROADMAP.md).

Why this catalog bypasses the LLM entirely for these 3 known cases,
rather than always going through ``pinneapple_llm.draft_problem``: manual
testing on 2026-09-16 against a local Ollama server (llama3.2:3b) showed
``draft_problem`` reliably PICKS the right preset for both new
descriptions below (6/6 independent calls each), but UNRELIABLY fills in
that preset's kwargs -- it frequently emits an explicit ``None`` for a
parameter it has no opinion on instead of omitting it (so the preset
factory falls back to its own documented default), which crashes the
preset factory instead of degrading gracefully:
``TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'NoneType' and
'NoneType'``. Measured failure rate across independent
``draft_problem()`` + ``get_preset()`` calls that day:
``axial_compressor_meanline`` 4/8 failed, ``axial_compressor_stage_3d``
6/8 failed. That is not an acceptable failure rate for a fixed demo case
a live commercial pitch depends on running every single time, so these 3
catalog entries carry a complete, explicit, never-``None`` kwargs dict
instead (the preset's own documented defaults, spelled out) and skip
``draft_problem`` altogether when selected via ``example_case=...``.

This is purely additive: a user's own free-form problem description
still goes through ``draft_problem`` exactly as before (see
``recommend.formulate_and_recommend``) -- ``example_case`` is an opt-in
shortcut for these 3 known-good cases only, not a replacement for the LLM
path in general.

**Why the two turbomachinery cases carry a non-default ``residual_threshold``,
measured, not guessed.** ``pinneapple_llm.guardrail.PhysicsGuardrail``'s
``pde_residual`` check compares a raw mean-squared PDE residual against a
single absolute number (``residual_threshold``, platform default ``1e-2``
-- calibrated for ``burgers_1d``, whose only field ``u`` is O(1) by
construction). ``axial_compressor_meanline``/``axial_compressor_stage_3d``
solve their PDE in raw SI units instead (temperatures ~300 K, pressures
~1e5 Pa) -- ``compile_problem`` (inside PINNeAPPle, out of this repo's
scope to change) does not non-dimensionalize those fields before computing
the residual, so its natural scale is ~1e3-1e8, not O(1). A real,
end-to-end measurement on 2026-09-16 (deterministic, ``solve_pde``'s own
fixed ``seed=0``) confirms this is a genuine unit-scale mismatch, not an
undertrained model: for ``axial_compressor_meanline``, an essentially
untrained model (10 epochs) has ``pde_residual`` ~1.26e8, a real, trained
model at this catalog's own epoch count (2000) reaches ~6.0e3, and even
10,000 epochs (145s -- too slow for a live demo) only reaches ~4.6e3 --
five more epochs of magnitude below ``1e-2`` is not reachable by training
longer, it is a scale artifact. The catalog below sets
``residual_threshold`` per turbomachinery case to a value that (a) a
genuinely well-trained model at this catalog's own ``epochs``/
``n_collocation`` clears with real margin, (b) an untrained/garbage model
misses by 3-4 orders of magnitude (so the check still meaningfully
discriminates), and (c) is documented here with the real numbers behind
it -- never picked to make one specific run's already-observed residual
pass after the fact.

(Extracted from Veriphysics' orchestrator; Apache-2.0 like the rest of PINNeAPPle. Execution queue, API and billing stay in Veriphysics.)

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.findings
children.doc:
Findings: each signal a validation run produced, explained without an LLM.

A number alone does not tell an engineer what to do. Every :class:`ValidationFinding` answers the same four questions, from
facts the run already produced and nothing else:

* **what happened** -- the observed value against the criterion that was configured, quoted from the record;
* **why it matters** -- what the criterion is for, in terms of the declared use;
* **what is still unknown** -- the causes this evidence cannot separate, stated rather than guessed;
* **what we recommend doing** -- next tests, in the order that would settle the doubt.

The text per rule lives in :data:`RULES` (a versioned table, not generated prose): the same input always gives the
same sentence, and every sentence points at the rule, the metric and the evidence that fired it. Nothing here decides
a status: :mod:`pinneapple_veriphysics.validation_case` turns findings into one, with a documented precedence.
Findings are never "pass" because a check was absent -- an absent check is a ``"not run"`` finding.

classes.name: FindingRule
classes.doc:
The fixed wording of one kind of finding. ``why`` and ``unknown`` are about the *rule*, not about a run: the
numbers of a particular run are quoted in ``ValidationFinding.what_happened``.

classes.name: ValidationFinding
classes.doc:
One explained signal. ``status`` is the outcome of the rule (fail / warning / not run / pass); the case, not
the finding, decides the status of the validation.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The four questions, in the order an engineer reads them.

functions.name: sort_findings
functions.sig: (findings: Sequence[ValidationFinding]) -> list[ValidationFinding]
functions.doc:
Failures first, then warnings, then not-run, then passes; ties keep the generation order (stable), so the same
case always numbers its findings the same way.

functions.name: build_findings
functions.sig: (*, profile: ValidationProfile, checks: Sequence[Any] = (), references: Sequence[Any] = (), uncertainty: Any = None, applicability: Any = None, provenance_problems: Sequence[str] = (), reviews: Sequence[Any] = (), critical_not_assessed: Sequence[str] = ()) -> list[ValidationFinding]
functions.doc:
Every finding the case's own contents justify, numbered ``VP-001``... in severity order.

The arguments are the plain records of a case (see :mod:`pinneapple_veriphysics.validation_case`); this function
reads them and quotes them, and computes nothing but comparisons of the numbers they carry.

children.summary: Findings: each signal a validation run produced, explained without an LLM.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.ledger
children.doc:
Evidence ledger: a test may be reported as passed only when a record shows that it ran.

Every entry holds what ran (``check_id``, ``tool``), on what (``inputs_sha256``: SHA-256 of the exact inputs),
what came out (``outputs``), when (``started_at`` / ``finished_at``, UTC ISO 8601) and its verdict (``passed``).
The entry is sealed with ``entry_sha256``, the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON, so a record edited after the fact
no longer counts.

:meth:`EvidenceLedger.status` is the only way reports in this package turn a check into words: ``"passed"`` or
``"failed"`` when a complete, intact entry exists, ``"not run"`` otherwise. A source that merely says a test
passed (a CI badge, a JSON without the record) is "not run" here::

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.ledger import EvidenceLedger, sha256_bytes

    ledger = EvidenceLedger()
    with ledger.run("residual", inputs_sha256=sha256_bytes(data), tool="my-check") as rec:
        rec.outputs = {"rel_residual": 3e-4}
        rec.passed = 3e-4 < 1e-3
    assert ledger.status("residual") == "passed"
    assert ledger.status("conservation") == "not run"

classes.name: EvidenceEntry
classes.doc: One recorded execution of a check. ``passed`` is None while it runs or when it crashed.

methods.name: problems
methods.doc: Why this entry cannot back a claim (empty when it can).

classes.name: EvidenceLedger
classes.doc:
An append-only list of :class:`EvidenceEntry`. Several entries may share a ``check_id`` (re-runs): the
status of a check is that of its latest valid entry.

methods.sig: (check_id: str, *, passed: bool, inputs_sha256: str, outputs: dict[str, Any], started_at: str, finished_at: str, name: str = '', category: str = '', tool: str = '', tool_version: str = '') -> EvidenceEntry
methods.doc: Record a check that already ran (times are those of the run, not of this call).

methods.name: run
methods.sig: (check_id: str, *, inputs_sha256: str, name: str = '', category: str = '', tool: str = '', tool_version: str = '') -> Iterator[EvidenceEntry]
methods.doc:
Time a check while it runs. Set ``rec.outputs`` and ``rec.passed`` inside the block; an exception is
recorded (no verdict, so the check reads "not run") and re-raised.

methods.name: latest
methods.doc: Latest valid entry of ``check_id`` (None if none).

methods.name: claim
methods.doc: One line a report may print about ``check_id``; "not run" unless the ledger proves otherwise.

functions.sig: (obj: Any) -> str
functions.doc: Sorted keys, no whitespace: the same object always gives the same bytes.

functions.sig: (data: bytes) -> str

functions.sig: (obj: Any) -> str

functions.sig: (path: str | Path, chunk: int = 1 << 20) -> str

functions.name: utc_now
functions.sig: (t: float | None = None) -> str

functions.sig: (ledger: EvidenceLedger, checks: Iterable[Any], *, prefix: str, inputs_sha256: str, started_at: str, finished_at: str, tool: str = '', tool_version: str = '') -> list[EvidenceEntry]
functions.doc:
Record the checks of a trust card (``pp.trust_card(...).checks`` or its ``to_dict()["checks"]``): one entry

entry, so it reads "not run".

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.maturity
children.doc:
Maturity and gap assessment: how far the evidence reaches, on two independent axes.

A single score hides what matters. A model can be excellent numerically and impossible to reproduce, or match a
benchmark and never have been evaluated in the conditions it will be operated in. So the assessment is a
multidimensional profile on two axes that are not forced to agree:

* **scientific maturity** -- quality of the evidence, methodological rigour, reproducibility and physical validation;
* **industrial readiness** -- fitness for the declared use, operational risk, controls and human authorization.

Five levels per axis (:data:`LEVELS`), each defined by *verifiable* requirements (:data:`REQUIREMENTS`) that facts of
the case either show or do not. A level is reached only when that level and every level below it are met: a good
average metric cannot lift a case past a missing reference, a missing reproducibility record or a missing review. The
scale is this package's own starting scale -- not an academic or industrial standard, and not a certification.

::

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.maturity import assess_maturity

    a = assess_maturity({"verification.residual_executed": True, "usecase.profile_defined": True, ...})
    print(a.render())                     # per axis: level reached, next level, the gaps with how to close each
    print(a.level("scientific"), a.gaps("scientific"))

classes.name: MaturityRequirement
classes.doc:
One verifiable requirement of one level of one axis. ``met_by`` is the key of the fact that shows it (see
:func:`assess_maturity`); ``how_to_meet`` is what produces that fact.

classes.name: AxisAssessment
classes.doc: Where one axis stands: the level reached, the one that is next, and what is missing for it.

classes.name: MaturityAssessment
classes.doc: The two axes, assessed independently, plus the facts they were read from.

methods.name: improvement_actions
methods.doc: The open requirements as concrete, ordered actions (a lower level first).

functions.name: requirements_for
functions.sig: (dimension: str, level: int | None = None) -> tuple[MaturityRequirement, ...]
functions.doc: The requirements of one axis (all levels, or one).

functions.name: assess_maturity
functions.sig: (facts: Mapping[str, bool] | Iterable[str]) -> MaturityAssessment
functions.doc:
Assess both axes from the facts of a case (``{fact key: True/False}``, or the keys that hold).

A fact that is absent is false: nothing is assumed to have happened because it usually does.

children.summary: Maturity and gap assessment: how far the evidence reaches, on two independent axes.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.mesh_views
children.doc:
3-D views of the reference comparisons of a Validation Lab run: for every result with a reference whose data is 3-D
and lives on a mesh (OpenFOAM case, VTU/VTK with cells), the prediction, the reference and the pointwise error on the
mesh, the regions with the largest error and the declared boundary conditions.

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.mesh_views import mesh_views
    for v in mesh_views(workdir, report=lab_dict):        # after run_validation(workdir)
        v["view"].glb(), v["view"].meta                    # pp.viz.field_view: for /shared/fieldview3d.js
        v["errors"]["U"]["hotspots"]                       # largest-error regions: centre, extent, max, share

The values are paired exactly as ``pinneapple check`` pairs them for PC701 (same files, same time, the reference
mapped to the result's points by nearest neighbour when the two differ), so the relative L2 shown is the PC701 number.
2-D results, point clouds without cells, tables and models get no 3-D view.

functions.name: mesh_views
functions.sig: (workdir: str | Path, config: str | Path | None = None, *, report: dict[str, Any] | None = None, max_faces: int | None = None, n_regions: int = 8, mesh_unit: str = 'm') -> list[dict[str, Any]]
functions.doc:
One view per 3-D result target with a reference: ``{"target", "view" (FieldView), "errors" {field: error map

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.model_grade
children.doc:
VeriPhysics grade of a model trained elsewhere (#1187): a field model ``u(x, t) -> fields`` (a PINN or neural
operator from any framework, through ONNX / TorchScript / a callable, or its predictions on points) graded against
the problem it claims to solve.

The problem is an equation system in the library's text grammar (:mod:`pinneapple_physics.symbolic_pde.text`, the
same one :mod:`pinneapple_problemdesign.formulate` writes) on a box, and/or reference data. Every check treats the
model as a black box: derivatives are central finite differences of its outputs (step ``fd_step`` of each axis'
span, second derivatives with the square-root step, nested for mixed ones), so it works for models whose framework
the library cannot differentiate.

Checks, each pass / fail / not applicable with its reason:

* ``grade.pde_residual``: each equation's residual at ``n_points`` fresh random points: its RMS over the RMS of the
  equation's largest term (a dimensionless relative residual) against ``residual_tol``; the finite-difference
  steps follow the model's output precision (``eps**(1/3)`` and ``eps**(1/4)`` of each span);
* ``grade.conditions``: each boundary / initial condition on its face, residual relative to the field's scale;
* ``grade.reference``: relative L2 error against reference data when given;
* ``grade.applicability``: the grading box inside the model's declared validity box;
* ``grade.robustness``: the output change for an input perturbation of ``eps`` of the span, against the change of
  the reference (or of the model itself at a finer perturbation: a smooth model scales linearly).

The decision follows a :class:`~pinneapple_veriphysics.policy.GradePolicy`: the user's (passed, named by
``PINNEAPPLE_VERIPHYSICS_POLICY`` or saved as their default) or the library's; tolerances passed to the call win
over the policy's. By default a failed critical check is REJECT, any other failure or a check that could not run
is REVIEW, and APPROVED needs every check to pass. The result records the policy it used.

Grade ``model(X) -> (N, n_fields)`` (``X`` columns in ``system.coords`` order) on the box ``bounds``.

``system``: a parsed :class:`~pinneapple_physics.symbolic_pde.text.EquationSystem` with its coefficients
given; ``reference``: ``(X_ref, U_ref)``; ``validity``: the model's declared validity box.

Grade a model known only by its predictions on scattered ``points`` (a results file): they are interpolated
by a local thin-plate-spline RBF (``scipy.interpolate.RBFInterpolator`` on the ``neighbors`` nearest points,
smooth enough for second derivatives) on coordinates scaled to the unit box, then graded like a model. A grade
of predictions is a grade of the predictions plus the interpolant: sparse or noisy points raise the residual.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.policy
children.doc:
The rules that turn checks into APPROVED / REVIEW / REJECT, set by the user (#1187).

The library ships a default (:data:`DEFAULT`); a user (or a team) sets their own and makes it their default:

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.policy import GradePolicy, save_policy, load_policy
    mine = GradePolicy(name="aero-team", residual_tol=0.01, reference_tol=0.02, inconclusive="reject")
    save_policy(mine)                    # ~/.config/pinneapple/veriphysics_policy.json: the default from now on
    load_policy()                        # -> mine;  load_policy("pinneapple-default") -> the library's

Which policy applies, first match wins: the one passed to the call (a :class:`GradePolicy`, a dict of its fields
or a JSON path), the file named by ``PINNEAPPLE_VERIPHYSICS_POLICY``, the user's saved default, the library default.
Every decision records the policy it used (its name and every field), so a grade can be reproduced.

Fields:

* tolerances of the model-grade checks (``residual_tol``, ``condition_tol``, ``reference_tol``,
  ``robustness_band``) and the finite-difference ``eps``;
* ``critical``: checks whose failure is REJECT; any other failure is REVIEW (``fail_noncritical="reject"`` makes
  every failure REJECT);
* ``inconclusive``: what a check that could not run does: ``"review"`` (the default), ``"ignore"`` or ``"reject"``;
  ``required``: checks that must have run (inconclusive there is REVIEW at least, whatever ``inconclusive`` says);
* ``min_coverage`` / ``min_score``: the share of checks that ran and the weighted share that passed
  (:class:`pinneapple_analysis.trust.trust_report.TrustReport` reads these too).

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.recommend
children.doc:
The "formulation + method intelligence" half of ``pipeline.analyze()``,
factored out so it can run on its own -- fast (no training, one
``draft_problem`` LLM call), for the "Solution Recommendation" screen:
internal solver/architecture choice and external tools/players, shown
side by side with real, documented pros/cons for every candidate
(never fabricated accuracy/cost numbers -- see ``tool_recommendation``/
``architecture_recommendation``'s own honesty-scope docstrings), BEFORE
committing to a real training run. ``pipeline.analyze()`` itself calls
this function too, so the two entry points can never silently disagree
about what formulation/method intelligence step 1-3 produced.

(Extracted from Veriphysics' orchestrator; Apache-2.0 like the rest of PINNeAPPle. Execution queue, API and billing stay in Veriphysics.)

score. ``is_recommended`` distinguishes the primary pick from an

catalog entry (``ARCHITECTURE_CATALOG`` / ``TOOL_CATALOG``).

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.robustness
children.doc:
Robustness studies that feed the applicability map with *measured*
evidence for the three items that used to be ``NOT_RUN``:

* :func:`extrapolation_study` -- generalization: the governing-equation
  residual, and (with an ensemble) the disagreement between independently
  trained models, on shells *outside* the training domain at growing
  margins. The largest margin where both stay acceptable is the measured
  extrapolation limit of the surrogate.
* :func:`ensemble_study` -- UQ: K extra seeds of the same architecture; the
  spread across members is an epistemic-uncertainty estimate. It is
  *uncalibrated* unless reference data is supplied
  (:func:`calibration_against_reference`).
* :func:`weight_sensitivity_study` -- loss weights: retrain with the PDE
  term up- and down-weighted and measure how much the prediction moves.

Everything here runs real training/evaluation and returns plain dicts of
the numbers it measured; nothing is estimated heuristically except the two
documented tolerances below. A residual that is small outside the domain
shows the surrogate still satisfies the PDE there -- it does NOT prove it
matches the true solution (boundary conditions do not constrain it), which
is why the ensemble spread is reported next to it and the map says so.

(Extracted from Veriphysics' orchestrator; Apache-2.0 like the rest of PINNeAPPle. Execution queue, API and billing stay in Veriphysics.)

functions.name: ensemble_study
functions.sig: (spec, build_model: Callable[[], Any], best_model, *, n_members: int, epochs: int, n_collocation: int, n_eval: int = 2048, margins: Sequence[float] = DEFAULT_MARGINS) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Train *n_members* extra seeds and measure member disagreement in the
interior and on each outside shell. Returns the models too (key
``"members"``) so callers can reuse them; strip before serializing.

functions.name: extrapolation_study
functions.sig: (spec, model, *, residual_threshold: float, ensemble: dict[str, Any] | None = None, margins: Sequence[float] = DEFAULT_MARGINS, n_eval: int = 2048, spread_tol: float = SPREAD_REL_TOL) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Residual (and ensemble spread, if given) on shells outside the
training box. ``supported_margin`` is the largest margin such that it
and every smaller margin keep residual <= threshold and spread <=
``spread_tol`` (default ``SPREAD_REL_TOL``); ``0.0`` means even the smallest shell fails.

functions.name: weight_sensitivity_study
functions.sig: (spec, build_model: Callable[[], Any], best_model, *, epochs: int, n_collocation: int, factors: Sequence[float] = DEFAULT_WEIGHT_FACTORS, n_eval: int = 2048, spread_tol: float = SPREAD_REL_TOL) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Retrain with ``w_pde`` scaled by each factor (other weights at their
defaults) and measure the RMS change of the prediction vs *best_model*
relative to the field's RMS magnitude. Note: the seed differs from the
original run's, so a part of the difference is seed noise -- compare
with the ensemble's ``interior_rel_spread``.

functions.name: calibration_against_reference
functions.sig: (members: Sequence[Any], reference_x, reference_y) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Real calibration of the ensemble against supplied reference data via
``CalibrationMetrics`` -- the only way to turn the spread into a
*calibrated* uncertainty. Returns ece/coverage/sharpness.

functions.name: condition_coverage
functions.sig: (spec, n: int = 50000) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
How many points each auto-sampled (``callable``/``all``) boundary,
initial or data condition selects under the SAME sampler the installed
``pinneapple_physics.solve_pde`` uses, so this reports what training
will actually enforce.

Current PINNeAPPle samples the faces of the domain box and raises when
a condition selects nothing (``condition_sampling.sample_condition_points``).
Older versions only drew uniform interior points and silently dropped a
condition like ``np.isclose(X[:, 1], 0.0)`` (the ``burgers_1d`` preset)
-- in that case this falls back to uniform sampling and reports it as
unenforced, which is exactly what that version's training did.
``tag`` conditions are reported as ``None`` (need real geometry).

functions.name: parameter_shift_study
functions.sig: (make_spec: Callable[..., Any], base_kwargs: dict[str, Any], build_model: Callable[[], Any], base_model, *, residual_threshold: float, epochs: int, n_collocation: int, shifts: Sequence[float] = DEFAULT_PARAM_SHIFTS, max_params: int = 2, n_eval: int = 2048, spread_tol: float = SPREAD_REL_TOL) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Parameter generalization: how far can a physical parameter move
before the surrogate trained at the base value stops being usable?

For each numeric parameter in *base_kwargs* (at most *max_params*) and
each relative *shift*, the problem is rebuilt with
``make_spec(**{param: value * (1 + shift)})`` and a FRESH model is
trained on it. That reference model is only a proxy for the truth, so it
is trusted only if its own PDE residual passes *residual_threshold*
(``reference_trusted``). The measured quantity is the RMS difference
between the base surrogate and the reference model on the same interior
points, relative to the reference field's RMS magnitude. A shift is ``ok``
when the reference is trusted and that difference is within
``spread_tol`` (default ``SPREAD_REL_TOL``); ``supported_shift`` is the largest shift for which it
and every smaller shift are ok. Costs ``len(shifts) * n_params``
trainings. Geometry changes are NOT covered (they need real geometry).

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.scope
children.doc:
Scope of use: which uses a result can serve, where it fails, and why -- beyond one approve / reject verdict.

A trust score says whether a result can be used; a reviewing engineer also needs to know *for what*: a surrogate can
be fine for field values away from the walls and wrong for the boundary fluxes of the same prediction. A
:class:`ScopeOfUse` lists each use with its verdict, the measured value against the limit, what the use needs, and
where the evidence comes from:

- ``certified``: a guaranteed bound (e.g. a residual-based error bound);
- ``estimated``: an estimate without a guarantee (e.g. an error map from the residual), shown with its validation;
- ``input check``: the inputs against the validated range -- a precondition of every use, not a use of its own;
- ``reference``: a comparison with a reference solution.

Like the rest of this package it computes nothing: it carries verdicts that the analysis code already produced
(for instance ``pinneapple_physics.darcy_checks.use_verdicts``) into the Decision Record and the Evidence Report.

The uses a result can and cannot serve, with an optional figure (a path to a PNG) and notes (for instance

A :class:`ScopeOfUse` from per-use verdicts ``{use: {"ok", "reason", "why", "values", "limits"}}`` (the form

A :class:`ScopeOfUse` over a batch of per-sample verdicts: a use is OK when at least ``min_fraction`` of the
samples serve it (0.9: nine in ten, the batch convention of ``pinneapple_physics.darcy_checks``); the share is
kept in ``fraction_ok`` and the reason quotes the median measured values.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.surrogate_gates
children.doc:
Gates on a *model*, not on its data: accuracy, conservation, boundary conditions and the PDE residual.

The gates in :mod:`pinneapple_data.schema.gates` ask whether a dataset is well-formed. These ask whether a trained
surrogate is worth believing, and they are the half the mapping calls "model-side": a network can reproduce a field
to three digits and still violate the equation it claims to solve, drift the quantity that should be conserved, or
ignore the wall it was given.

Four gates, each with a number and a tolerance:

``accuracy``
    relative L2 against the reference over the held-out region.
``conservation``
    the spatial integral of a conserved field, along the time axis, on the **prediction** -- and the same measure on
    the data. Reporting only the model's drift hides the case where the reference itself leaks; reporting both lets
    a reviewer see which of the two moved.
``boundary``
    for every Dirichlet condition the bundle declares on a structured bundle's edge (``region="x_low"``), the mean
    deviation of the predicted values there from the declared value, relative to the field's own scale.
``residual``
    the governing equation's residual evaluated on the prediction by finite differences, normalised by the size of
    its own terms, so the number is "how much of the equation's own magnitude is left unbalanced" rather than a
    number whose size depends on the units.

Nothing here is imported from the data layer: a bundle is duck-typed (``.manifest``, ``.field_array``, ``.axes``,
``.array``), so this module keeps the property the rest of the package has -- it holds no physics of its own and no
dependency it does not need.

    >>> from pinneapple_veriphysics.surrogate_gates import run_surrogate_gates
    >>> report = run_surrogate_gates(predicted, reference=data, field="density", conserved="density",
    ...                              equation="burgers", parameters={"nu": 0.01})
    >>> print(report.summary())

A gate that cannot be asked (no boundary condition declared, no equation named) is "not run", never "passed" --
the same rule the evidence ledger applies to everything else in this package.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.usecase
children.doc:
Use-case specification: what "success" means, before any verification runs.

A model is not good or bad in the abstract. A surrogate whose error is 8 % is useless for a paper that reports 0.5 % and
may be perfectly adequate to triage industrial designs -- and a low *mean* error can still be unacceptable when it
sits in the region the decision depends on. So the first object of a validation case is not a test but a declaration:
the intended use, the quantity that decides it, the tolerance that use needs, which independent reference exists, and
what happens if the decision is wrong.

:class:`ValidationProfile` carries that declaration. Everything here is *configured by the caller*: the tolerance is
a requirement, not a measurement, and choosing one never proves that a model meets it. :data:`OBJECTIVES` records
starting points that practitioners commonly quote (a fraction of a percent for a rigorous research comparison, single
digits to low teens of a percent for engineering triage) and says so -- they are illustrative, not norms, and not a
substitute for the tolerance the intended use actually requires.

::

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.usecase import PROFILE_PRESETS

    profile = PROFILE_PRESETS["industrial_screening"]
    print(profile.describe())            # what this profile requires, and what it cannot require
    print(profile.problems())            # ["no independent reference declared: ..."] when incomplete

classes.name: ValidationProfile
classes.doc:
The declared use of a result. Immutable: changing the use means a new profile, and a new case.

``target_error_pct``: the largest error the intended use accepts, in percent, for ``primary_metric``. It is a
requirement. ``reference_evidence``: kinds of independent evidence the use needs (see :data:`REFERENCE_KINDS`).
``critical_quantities`` / ``critical_regions``: the quantities and places the decision depends on; a global mean
error says nothing about them. ``consequence``: one of :data:`CONSEQUENCES`.

methods.name: needs_independent_reference
methods.doc: An objective that claims validation has to be backed by something independent of the model's own loss.

methods.name: problems
methods.doc: Why this profile cannot yet support a validation claim (empty when it can). Never a score.

methods.name: describe
methods.doc: Deterministic explanation of what this profile requires and what it does not claim.

methods.name: with_changes
methods.doc: A new profile with ``changes`` applied (the case history then shows two profiles, not one edited one).

functions.name: profile_presets
functions.sig: () -> list[str]
functions.doc: Names of the ready-made profiles (each still has to be confirmed for the actual use).

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.validation_case
children.doc:
Validation case: one prediction, the evidence behind it, the decision about it, and the history of that decision.

The unit of the validation loop is not a score but a *case*: a model version, a reproducible physical problem, the
checks that actually ran, the reference comparisons, the measured domain of applicability, the uncertainty, an expert
decision with its scope, and an append-only history of all of it. A case is created by :meth:`ValidationCase.open` and
only ever evolves by appending a revision -- reviewing, attaching evidence or re-running checks produces a new
revision, never an edit of the old one. Every revision stores the snapshot it sealed, so tampering is detectable
(:meth:`ValidationCase.history_problems`).

The status of a case is one of :data:`STATUSES`, decided by the documented precedence in :meth:`ValidationCase.decide`
from the findings (:mod:`pinneapple_veriphysics.findings`) of the evidence actually present:

``failed``         a mandatory check failed, a reference comparison exceeded the declared tolerance, or an expert
                   refused the use;
``unvalidated``    the evidence the declared profile requires has not been produced (nothing ran, a required check
                   or an independent reference is missing);
``review required`` evidence exists but carries flags (extrapolation, uncalibrated uncertainty, an incomplete
                   requirement) or the expert decision that authorizes use is still missing;
``validated``      the requirements hold *and* an authorized expert approved the use inside a documented scope.

Absence of alerts is never a pass: the checks are not run by this module, and a case with nothing recorded is
``unvalidated`` by construction.

::

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.validation_case import ValidationCase, ModelVersion, ProblemRef, CheckVerdict

    case = ValidationCase.open(profile=profile, model=ModelVersion("pinn", "v3", checkpoint_sha256=sha),
                               problem=ProblemRef("heat 2-D", pde="poisson"), requested_use="screening at 95 C",
                               actor="analyst")
    case = case.with_checks([CheckVerdict("PDE residual", "verification", True, 3e-3, 1e-2)], actor="analyst")
    print(case.assess().render())            # findings, maturity on both axes, status and why

classes.name: ModelVersion
classes.doc:
What exactly produced the prediction: a name, a version and an identifiable artefact (checkpoint hash) or the
configuration that rebuilds it. Without one of the two the case cannot say which model it validated.

classes.name: ProblemRef
classes.doc: The physical problem the prediction answers, described well enough to rebuild it.

classes.name: RunProvenance
classes.doc:
What reproducing these numbers requires: which tool ran, on which version, over which inputs, with which seeds
and tolerances. ``problems()`` lists what is missing -- an incomplete record is a finding, never a silent gap.

classes.name: ProcessControls
classes.doc:
The controls an operational use needs: who owns the result, what is monitored, what happens when the model
leaves its scope, and how a change of model re-opens the validation.

classes.name: CheckVerdict
classes.doc:
The verdict of one check, as the tool that ran it recorded it. ``passed is None`` means the check did not run,
and it stays "not run" -- never a neutral pass.

classes.name: ReferenceComparison
classes.doc:
A comparison of the prediction against evidence independent of it: the acceptance criterion of the declared
use, expressed as ``value_pct`` (the measured error, percent) against ``tolerance_pct`` (the accepted one).

classes.name: UncertaintyEvidence
classes.doc:
A measured uncertainty and, explicitly, whether it was calibrated. An uncalibrated spread is a disagreement
bar (it detects instability); it is not a confidence interval and cannot bound the error.

classes.name: ApplicabilityFacts
classes.doc:
What the applicability evidence says about the condition the use asks for: the ranges that were verified and
which of the requested inputs fall outside them.

classes.name: ExpertReview
classes.doc:
A decision taken by a person about the evidence in the case. It never overwrites the technical results: it is
recorded next to them, with its justification and -- for an approval -- the scope it applies to.

methods.name: covers
methods.doc:
Whether this decision applies to ``requested_use``. A scope that names no use covers the case as assessed;
a scope that names uses covers only those (a validated range is not a validated use outside it).

methods.name: record
methods.sig: (reviewer: str, decision: str, justification: str, *, role: str = '', scope: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, evidence_ids: Sequence[str] = ()) -> ExpertReview
methods.doc: A review stamped with the current UTC time and a stable id (``reviewer`` + ``decided_at`` + decision).

classes.name: Revision
classes.doc:
One sealed state of a case. ``snapshot`` is what the case looked like after the change; ``snapshot_sha256``
seals it, so an edited history no longer verifies.

classes.name: CaseAssessment
classes.doc: The state of a case, computed from its own contents: findings, maturity on both axes, status and the reason.

classes.name: ValidationCase
classes.doc: One validation case. Immutable: every change returns a new case with a new :class:`Revision` appended.

methods.name: open
methods.sig: (*, profile: ValidationProfile, model: ModelVersion, problem: ProblemRef, requested_use: str = '', actor: str = '', title: str = '') -> ValidationCase
methods.doc:
A new case, sealed as revision 1. ``case_id`` derives from the profile, the model and the problem, so the
same case re-opened with the same inputs is recognisable.

methods.name: with_checks
methods.sig: (checks: Sequence[CheckVerdict], *, action: str = 'checks recorded', actor: str = '', note: str = '') -> ValidationCase
methods.doc: Attach the verdicts of a verification run (they replace the previous set, which stays in the history).

methods.name: with_reference
methods.sig: (reference: ReferenceComparison, *, actor: str = '', note: str = '') -> ValidationCase

methods.name: with_review
methods.doc: Record an expert decision as a new revision (previous decisions stay in the history).

methods.name: critical_not_assessed
methods.doc:
Declared critical quantities/regions that no evidence in the case covers (a reference comparison whose
measured quantity is the critical one counts as covering it).

methods.name: facts
methods.doc: Every fact the maturity assessment reads, with the value this case actually supports.

methods.name: assess
methods.doc: Findings, maturity and status of this case, computed from its contents only.

methods.name: decide
methods.sig: (findings: Sequence[ValidationFinding]) -> tuple[str, str, str, Mapping[str, Any] | None, list[str]]
methods.doc: The status policy, in documented precedence order. A reviewer cannot overwrite a technical failure.

methods.name: history_problems
methods.doc: Why the stored history cannot be trusted (empty when every revision still verifies).

classes.name: ValidationRegistry
classes.doc:
The evidence registry of a team: every case (latest revision), queried by model, by status and by use, plus the
improvement tasks derived from the gaps -- so a confirmed failure or a missing evidence becomes an action rather
than a footnote.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
Store a case. A new revision of a known case replaces its previous state; the case itself carries the
history of both.

methods.name: evidence_rows
methods.doc: Flat view of every piece of evidence, with the case and verdict it belongs to (the auditable index).

methods.name: tasks
methods.doc:
Improvement tasks, derived deterministically from what each case lacks (never invented): the open maturity
requirements, a refused use, and the evidence a reviewer asked for.

methods.name: save
methods.doc: Write the registry as JSON (cases keep their full history) and return the file's SHA-256.

functions.name: checks_from_trust_card
functions.sig: (card: Any) -> tuple[CheckVerdict, ...]
functions.doc:
The checks of ``pinneapple_analysis.trust.trust_card`` (a ``FieldTrustCard``, its ``.checks`` list, or their
``to_dict()`` form) as :class:`CheckVerdict`.

functions.name: checks_from_lab_report
functions.sig: (report: Mapping[str, Any] | Any) -> tuple[CheckVerdict, ...]
functions.doc: The outcomes of a Validation Lab run (``LabReport.to_dict()``, or a ``LabReport``) as :class:`CheckVerdict`.

functions.name: checks_from_ledger
functions.sig: (ledger: EvidenceLedger) -> tuple[CheckVerdict, ...]
functions.doc:
The latest valid entry of every check in an :class:`~pinneapple_veriphysics.ledger.EvidenceLedger`. A check with
no valid entry is reported once as "not run" -- never dropped.

functions.name: applicability_facts_from_map
functions.sig: (amap: Mapping[str, Any] | Any, query: Mapping[str, float] | None = None, *, requested_condition: str = '') -> ApplicabilityFacts
functions.doc:
Extrapolation detection from an ``applicability.build_applicability_map(...).to_dict()`` and the inputs the use
actually asks for: every queried variable outside its verified range lands in ``outside_variables``.

The range is widened by the *measured* extrapolation margin when the study established one; without a measured
margin nothing outside the verified range is supported.

children.summary: Validation case: one prediction, the evidence behind it, the decision about it, and the history of that decision.

children.name: pinneapple_veriphysics.validation_lab
children.doc:
Validation Lab: run the physics checks of ``pinneapple check`` on predictions, results or a zoo model and
report them in three separate groups, with an evidence record for every check that ran.

=========================  ==============================================================================
``verification``           Numerical verification: were the equations solved right? PDE residuals, finite
                           values, readable and intact artefacts, method status in the catalog.
``validation``             Validation against data: does the answer match a trusted reference, and is the
                           model used where data backs it? Reference regression, QoIs, applicability (OOD).
``physics``                Physical consistency: conservation, boundary and initial conditions, bounds and
                           physical constraints, dimensional consistency (units), dataset physics.
=========================  ==============================================================================

No single test, nor all of them together, guarantees that a model represents reality: the report says so
(:data:`DISCLAIMER`) and lists, per target, the groups in which nothing ran.

::

    from pinneapple_veriphysics.validation_lab import config_from_spec, run_validation

    toml = config_from_spec({"results": [{"path": "T.npz", "physics": "heat", "units": {"T": "K"}}]})
    (work / "pinneapple-check.toml").write_text(toml)
    report = run_validation(work)
    report.to_dict()                 # JSON: categories, outcomes, provenance, evidence ledger
    render_html(report.to_dict())    # self-contained HTML

The configuration written to the report reproduces the run: ``pinneapple check --config pinneapple-check.toml``.

classes.name: CodeNotAllowed
classes.doc: The configuration would import or unpickle user-supplied code.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: Per group: counts and, per target, what ran or that nothing did.

functions.name: category_of
functions.sig: (rule_id: str) -> str | None
functions.doc: Group of a ``pinneapple check`` rule (None for PC002, which is about coverage, not a check).

functions.name: to_toml
functions.sig: (doc: dict[str, Any]) -> str
functions.doc:
Write a ``pinneapple-check.toml``: ``check`` as a table, ``result``/``model``/``dataset`` as arrays of
tables, nested values as inline tables. Only what the configuration needs (no dates, no nulls).

functions.name: model_ref_target
functions.sig: (ref: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

functions.name: config_from_spec
functions.sig: (spec: dict[str, Any]) -> str
functions.doc:
``pinneapple-check.toml`` from a plain description of what to check::

    {"results": [{"path": "pred.npz", "physics": "heat", "parameters": {"k": "10 W/(m*K)"},
                  "units": {"T": "K"}, "bounds": {"T": [250, 400]}, "bc": {"x=max": {"T": 300}},
                  "reference": {"path": "ref.npz", "rel-l2": 0.01}, "tolerances": {"residual": 0.05}}],
     "models": [{"zoo": "heatsink_forced_mlp"}],
     "select": ["ALL"], "fail_on": "error"}

Keys of each result are those of ``[[result]]`` in ``pinneapple check`` (``_`` or ``-``).

functions.name: assert_no_code
functions.sig: (cfg) -> None
functions.doc:
Refuse targets that execute code from the inputs: a ``file.py:function`` or checkpoint model, a Hub
download. Zoo models (shipped with the library, hashes checked) and data files are allowed.

functions.name: write_inputs
functions.sig: (root: str | Path, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> list[str]
functions.doc:
Write uploaded files (``{relative path: bytes}``, e.g. from ``pinneapple_data.cae.upload.expand``) under
``root``; a name that would land outside ``root`` is refused.

functions.name: tables_to_csv
functions.sig: (root: str | Path, config_text: str | None = None) -> tuple[str | None, dict[str, str]]
functions.doc:
Parquet files and JSON tables (a list of row objects, or an object of equal-length columns) under ``root``
become CSV next to them, which ``pinneapple check`` reads as point clouds or quantities of interest. Returns the
configuration with the references renamed and ``{old: new}``. Other JSON (manifests, reports) is left alone.

functions.name: run_validation
functions.sig: (workdir: str | Path, config: str | Path | None = None, *, allow_code: bool = False, title: str = 'Validation') -> LabReport
functions.doc:
Run ``pinneapple check`` on the inputs under ``workdir`` with ``config`` (default
``workdir/pinneapple-check.toml``) and record every outcome in an evidence ledger.

functions.name: summarize
functions.sig: (lab: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc: Compact view of a lab report dict: decision, per-group counts and groups that did not run.

functions.name: render_html
functions.sig: (lab: dict[str, Any]) -> str
functions.doc: Self-contained HTML of a lab report dict (no scripts, no external files).

children.summary: Validation Lab: run the physics checks of pinneapple check on predictions, results or a zoo model and report them in three separate groups, with an evidence record for every check that ran.

doc:
pinneapple_veriphysics — the verification and evidence layer of Veriphysics, as part of PINNeAPPle.

What a run produces and how it is reported, built only from objects the analysis modules already computed (no number or verdict
of its own):

=========================  ==============================================================================================
``decision``               ``DecisionRecord``: recommendation, trust score and coverage, per-check evidence, alternatives
``evidence_report``        the Evidence Report as a PDF (needs the optional ``reportlab``)
``applicability``          the applicability map: evidence chain, 8-item checklist and the variable envelope that was tested
``scope``                  the scope of use: which uses a result serves, where it fails and why (beyond approve / reject)
``robustness``             measured robustness studies (does the verdict survive perturbing the problem?)
``recommend``              formulate a problem and recommend a solver family and architecture from the verification catalog
``execution_log``          a collector for what each step did (shown next to the result)
``example_cases``          worked example problems for the recommender
``ledger``                 the evidence ledger: a check reads "passed" only with an intact record of its run
``validation_lab``         ``pinneapple check`` grouped into numerical verification, validation against data and
                           physical consistency, with a ledger entry per outcome (the Validation Lab app)
``evidence_package``       engineering evidence report (HTML, PDF) and zip package from other tools' outputs
``usecase``                the use-case specification: decision, decision quantity, tolerance and consequence
``findings``               each signal explained (what happened / why it matters / what is unknown / what to do next)
``maturity``               maturity and gap assessment on two axes: scientific maturity and industrial readiness
``validation_case``        the validation case, its append-only revisions, expert reviews and the evidence registry
``dossier``                the validation dossier: the case as the document an engineer files and a reviewer signs
``surrogate_gates``        accuracy, conservation, boundary conditions and the PDE residual of a *trained model*
=========================  ==============================================================================================

Veriphysics (the product) keeps the job queue, the HTTP API, billing and the web app, and imports this package.
summary: The verification and evidence layer of Veriphysics, as part of PINNeAPPle.
